condition: Rial price of one US dollar in the exchange market
what_varies: the number of rials a US dollar buys or sells for (buying and selling where given, or an average over a stated period)
note: Joins parts B, C, D and E. Rows that also give the Saudi riyal's price (YQ-C391, YQ-E079, YQ-E080, YQ-E584, YQ-E585, YQ-E870, YQ-E871) are here for their US dollar price; YQ-E447 also reports a dollar shortage. Rates a central bank sets, caps or publishes, data providers' quotes, and descriptions without a figure are separate conditions, since they hold together with a market price.

condition: Rial price of one Saudi riyal in the exchange market
what_varies: the number of rials a Saudi riyal buys or sells for (buying and selling where given, or an average)
note: Part D only. Rows giving both currencies are in the US dollar condition.

condition: Rial rate of the US dollar that a central bank sets, caps or publishes
what_varies: the official rate: the rate a central bank fixes, the highest selling price it approves, or the rate it publishes
note: Joins parts B, D and E. YQ-E409, YQ-E599 and YQ-E600 also give the Saudi riyal's fixed rate, and YQ-E599 the black-market rates of the same day. YQ-D236 to YQ-D260 are the rates the Central Bank in Aden published on its currency-history page.

condition: Rial rate of the Saudi riyal that a central bank sets or caps
what_varies: the official rate a central bank fixes, or the highest selling price it approves
note: Joins parts B, D and E.

condition: Price in Saudi riyals at which a US dollar is sold, as a central bank states it
what_varies: the number of Saudi riyals per US dollar

condition: Whether the authority fixes and enforces the exchange rate, or lets it float
what_varies: fixed or capped and enforced by the central bank or authorities, or floating with the market
note: Joins parts C, D and E: whether banks and exchange businesses must deal at a rate the authority sets. The rate's figure is in the rate conditions.

condition: How the rial's exchange rate is moving
what_varies: stable, fluctuating, falling or improving
note: Descriptions without a figure, which hold together with a price.

condition: Whether the market exchange rate differs from the official rate
what_varies: whether, and how far, the market rate diverges from the official rate
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Whether every exchanger deals at the same rate
what_varies: the same rate everywhere, or rates that differ from shop to shop

condition: Rial rate of the US dollar that international data providers quote
what_varies: the quoted rate
note: Data providers' quotes (Trading Economics, Wise) whose sources say neither where nor by whom the rate is used; they are far from the market prices of the same days, so they are a separate condition.

condition: How the central bank supplies foreign currency for imports
what_varies: the mechanism (financing from reserves, the substitution mechanism, Saudi-deposit letters of credit, currency auctions, the import committee's approvals) and whether it is running, curtailed or suspended
note: Joins parts A, D and E, including part D's 'how imports are regulated and financed' (the National Committee for Regulating and Financing Imports). YQ-D235 and YQ-E690 are the same undated headline.

condition: What foreign currency bought at the central bank's auctions may be used for
what_varies: the uses allowed

condition: Whether banks and importers may take part in the Aden central bank's currency auctions
what_varies: allowed or banned

condition: Where importers obtain foreign currency
what_varies: the main source: banks and the central bank, money exchangers, the parallel market, or remittances
note: Joins parts D and E. The central bank's own supply mechanism is a separate condition, since both hold together.

condition: How available foreign currency is
what_varies: ample, scarce or severely short
note: Joins parts D and E. Part D's capped access to foreign currency (YQ-D402) is a limit, in the condition on buying foreign currency.

condition: Whether exchange businesses may buy and sell foreign currency
what_varies: allowed, barred from selling to merchants or importers, or suspended

condition: Whether foreign currency may be bought and sold through digital platforms
what_varies: allowed, or cash transactions only

condition: What the central bank does to banks and exchange companies that speculate in foreign currency
what_varies: the measures and penalties

condition: How much foreign currency a person can sell for rials
what_varies: the daily ceiling banks and exchangers apply, or refusal to convert

condition: How much foreign currency a person may buy
what_varies: the cap on purchases and what must be shown
note: Joins parts D and E: the caps on access to foreign currency the Central Bank in Aden set in August 2025.

condition: How much foreign currency exchange companies may hold
what_varies: what they must do with surplus foreign currency

condition: Exchange rate customs uses to assess duty
what_varies: the rials per US dollar used, and the goods it applies to
note: YQ-E347 and YQ-E485 give different rates for 2025 (750 and 700); YQ-E377 gives the rate for luxury and non-essential goods.

condition: Currency in which banks settle import payments
what_varies: the currency

condition: Which rial banknote prints may be used for payment, and by whom
what_varies: which prints are allowed or banned (notes printed before 2016, notes the Aden central bank printed after 2016, or particular new denominations) and for which parties (banks, exchange firms, traders, the public)
note: Joins parts A to E, including part B's conditions split by the parties barred (banks and exchange firms, YQ-B028, YQ-B031; importers, wholesalers, malls and fuel stations, YQ-B029) and part D's merchant's own rule (YQ-D296). Bans on particular parties and denominations are states of who may use which notes. What holders of withdrawn notes must do, and the coins and 200-rial notes issued from 2024, are separate conditions.

condition: What holders of banknotes withdrawn from use must do with them
what_varies: where and by when they must hand the notes in, who may, and what they get for them
note: Joins parts A to D.

condition: Whether the new 50- and 100-rial coins and 200-rial notes may be used for payment
what_varies: which coin or note, who issued it, and whether it is issued and circulating, refused, or declared illegal
note: Joins parts A, C, D and E. Kept apart from the prints condition because these coins and notes circulate alongside the pre-2016 notes. YQ-A004 and YQ-A005 name no seat for the central bank; YQ-E605 concerns the 200-rial note the bank in Aden issued.

condition: Whether the central bank in Aden is issuing new banknotes
what_varies: whether new notes are being printed or a new issue approved, and how much

condition: Whether worn or damaged banknotes are accepted in payment
what_varies: accepted, or refused by merchants and in daily trade
note: Joins parts B to E.

condition: How much of the cash in circulation is usable
what_varies: the share of notes that are sound or damaged, and which denominations are affected
note: Joins parts C and E. Part C's YQ-C450 and YQ-C464 were worded with the problems of paying in banknotes; they give the share of sound notes.

condition: Problems of paying in cash
what_varies: the problems named (damaged notes, change, counting, sorting, moving and the risks of carrying cash)
note: Drawbacks of cash that payment providers name on their own pages.

condition: How available rial cash is
what_varies: ample, short or in crisis, and in which notes
note: Joins parts B to E. Sources disagree for Aden in February 2026 (YQ-D066, YQ-E602, YQ-E603).

condition: Whether one currency and one central bank serve the whole country
what_varies: one currency and central bank, or two (with notes accepted only in part of the country and two exchange rates)
note: Joins parts D and E. Also part E's 'Monetary authority over banks and payments' and part D's YQ-D206, which state the same split of the central bank; YQ-E724 and YQ-D540 report it in the same words.

condition: Currency in which domestic sales and contracts must be paid
what_varies: the rial only, or whether a seller may require or a buyer may use foreign currency, and the exceptions
note: Joins parts A, B, D and E. YQ-A019, YQ-A020, YQ-E730 and YQ-E848 report the Council of Ministers decision No. 13 of 2025 under different place names; YQ-E631 and YQ-E889 its implementation by the Ministry of Justice.

condition: Currency in which government fees are charged
what_varies: the currency of the fee

condition: Which currencies buyers and sellers use in everyday dealings
what_varies: the rial, or foreign currencies such as the Saudi riyal and the US dollar
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Main foreign currency of exchange transactions
what_varies: the currency most traded on the money market
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Currency used in trade between areas held by different parties
what_varies: the currency

condition: Whether the electronic rial may be used for payment
what_varies: available and for what, or warned against for banks, exchangers and businesses
note: Joins parts D and E: the e-rial's use where it is offered and the Aden central bank's warnings against dealing in it. YQ-E187 says e-rials were not widely accepted in 2019.

condition: Whether electronic balances trade at par with cash
what_varies: at par, or priced apart

condition: Amount of currency circulating outside the banking system
what_varies: the amount

condition: Which banks parties may deal with
what_varies: which banks are barred (the list each decision or designation names), for which parties, or that the bans were cancelled
note: Joins parts A to E: the central banks' decisions in Sana'a and Aden to stop dealing with named banks, their cancellation in July 2024, and the US designations of Yemeni banks, which bar US persons from dealing with them. Part A's 'Banks a party may deal with' is kept whole; the barred parties are named in each state. YQ-E823 also names US-sanctioned exchange companies, and YQ-E274 also bars traders from the Aden central bank's auctions. Also the suspension and revocation of the six Sana'a-headquartered banks' licences in July 2024, the Sana'a central bank's suspension of 13 Aden banks (YQ-E530), and the agreement of 23 July 2024 cancelling both sides' measures (YQ-E587, YQ-E721, YQ-E794). Sources date the measures against the six banks to May, 3 July and 10 July 2024.

condition: What parties barred from dealing with a bank must do with their balances there
what_varies: the deadline and what must be reported
note: Part B: exchange firms and transfer networks (YQ-B008) and financial institutions (YQ-B012), on the same decision.

condition: Whether banks the central bank has stopped dealing with must keep serving the public
what_varies: must keep serving customers, or not

condition: Which exchange companies parties may deal with
what_varies: which exchange companies are barred, suspended or restored (the list each decision, circular or designation names), and for whom
note: Joins parts A, B and D: the Sana'a side's bans and the US designations of Yemeni exchange companies. Also the central banks' suspensions, revocations and restorations of exchange businesses' licences and dealings, and the exchangers' association's circulars (parts C, D and E). YQ-E866 reports the same circular as YQ-B009, and YQ-E689, YQ-D234 and YQ-C075 the same undated headlines.

condition: Which e-wallets and e-payment services banks and exchange companies may deal with
what_varies: licensed ones only, with the unlicensed services named, or the ban lifted
note: Joins parts C to F: the Aden central bank's warning about Mobile Money (2020), its circular of 26 June 2024 on twelve named wallets, and that ban's reversal (YQ-D109).

condition: Whether parties may deal with Ansarallah (the Houthis)
what_varies: the designations Ansarallah carries (Foreign Terrorist Organization, Specially Designated Global Terrorist, EU listing, a group classified as terrorist), or their revocation
note: Joins parts A, D and E: US designations and their revocation in 2021, the EU listing, and the Aden central bank's sanction of banks for dealing with a group it calls classified as terrorist. Sources disagree on the date of the 2025 FTO designation (YQ-D490 in another condition, YQ-D553, YQ-D557, YQ-E007, YQ-E295).

condition: Which other Yemeni parties are under US sanctions
what_varies: the companies, individuals, vessels and crypto addresses each designation names
note: Joins parts A, D and E: designations other than banks, exchange companies and Ansarallah itself.

condition: Which transactions involving Ansarallah US persons may carry out under general licences
what_varies: the transactions each set of general licences authorizes

condition: Whether foreign financial institutions risk US secondary sanctions for dealings in Yemen
what_varies: the risk, and for which transactions
note: Joins parts A and E.

condition: What financial institutions must do with funds of persons listed for freezing
what_varies: freeze and report, under which list
note: Joins parts A, B and E: the UN assets freeze, the Yemeni anti-money-laundering law and the US rule for funds of designated groups.

condition: Whether US sanctions allow trade with the Yemeni people
what_varies: the stated scope of the designation

condition: Whether sending money to Yemen is lawful under US rules
what_varies: allowed, and for which recipients

condition: Whether US sanctions limit e-commerce in Yemen
what_varies: a limit, or not

condition: What financial institutions must do when serving customers to counter money laundering
what_varies: the due-diligence duties

condition: What financial institutions must do with a suspicious transaction
what_varies: the reporting duty
note: Also a wallet provider's terms on reporting suspected activity (YQ-C125).

condition: Whether banks and exchange companies must screen customers against sanctions lists
what_varies: required, which lists, and what to do on a match
note: Joins parts D and F: both rest on the Aden central bank's circular No. 4 of 2025.

condition: Yemen's standing with the FATF
what_varies: on the grey list or not

condition: Due diligence foreign financial institutions apply to Yemen
what_varies: risk-based, enhanced, or transactions ceased

condition: Which companies parties may deal with under the Houthi authorities' own sanctions
what_varies: the parties the Houthi authorities sanction

condition: Whether banks must move their head offices to Aden
what_varies: required or not, the deadline and the penalty, and whether the measures were withdrawn
note: Joins parts A, C, D and E: the Aden central bank's directives. Where banks' head offices actually are is a separate condition, since both hold together.

condition: Where banks' head offices and operations are
what_varies: in Sana'a or in Aden, and which banks have moved, decided to move or refused
note: Joins parts C, D and E, including part D's 'where financial institutions are based' (YQ-D397), which part D kept apart.

condition: Whether banks' branches are open to customers
what_varies: open and serving as usual, closed or ordered to cease by an authority, reopened, or closed by the bank, for the banks named
note: Joins parts C and E.

condition: How many branches a bank has, and where
what_varies: the number of branches and agents and the cities named
note: Joins parts C, D and E. YQ-C397 is the page of the bank its footer names Kuraimi Islamic Bank (kibanks.com); YQ-D608 and YQ-E638 name Kuraimi Bank and Al-Kuraimi.

condition: Bank branch opening hours
what_varies: the hours

condition: What it took a bank to reopen branches the authorities closed
what_varies: what was paid or agreed

condition: Where formal banking services are available
what_varies: concentrated in cities or reaching rural areas, the main centres, and how dense branches and service points are
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Businesses' access to a functioning bank branch
what_varies: the share of firms with access

condition: How many banks operate
what_varies: the number and kinds of banks
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Whether depositors can draw their bank deposits
what_varies: free to draw, frozen (for deposits made before the split or at a named bank), partly repaid, or banks unable to pay
note: Joins parts A, B, D and E. YQ-A037 and YQ-E894 report the same article.

condition: How much cash a bank customer can withdraw a day
what_varies: the daily ceiling, or that withdrawals are restricted
note: Joins parts C, D and E. Kept apart from frozen deposits: a daily ceiling on new withdrawals holds together with frozen old deposits.

condition: Whether depositors are rushing to withdraw from banks
what_varies: a rush of withdrawals, or not
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Where merchants and households keep their savings
what_varies: in banks, with exchange companies, or in gold
note: Joins parts A and D.

condition: Whether banks can draw their balances at the central bank
what_varies: free or restricted

condition: Whether banks can pay the salaries of organisations and companies they serve
what_varies: able or unable
note: Joins parts A and E; both report the same article.

condition: Whether interest-bearing transactions are allowed
what_varies: allowed, or banned by law (and from when, and how far applied)
note: Joins parts B, D and E. Sources date the Sana'a side's law to 2022 (YQ-E802) and 2023; YQ-B063 reports the bill's passage by the House of Representatives in Sana'a.

condition: Whether banks can reach SWIFT
what_varies: connected, cut off or non-functional, for the central bank or the banks named
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Whether bank accounts in Yemen use IBAN
what_varies: in use, or not

condition: Whether the central bank takes part in the Buna regional payment platform
what_varies: joined, or refuses
note: YQ-E597 also says IBAN was activated. Part D's YQ-D378 says Yemen has joined Buna.

condition: Whether Yemeni banks have correspondent banking relationships
what_varies: kept, limited, or severed, and with whom
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: What banks must do to keep access to international payments
what_varies: the requirement (SWIFT Scope, proof of relocation to Aden, compliance with the Aden central bank)
note: Joins parts D and E. YQ-D490 dates the US designation of the Houthis to 3 March 2025.

condition: Which banks a central bank treats as compliant
what_varies: the lists each central bank issues

condition: Which central bank's licence and rules banks are subject to
what_varies: the Sana'a central bank's, the Aden central bank's, or both
note: Joins parts A, C and D.

condition: Which central bank banks must report their data to
what_varies: the Aden central bank, or barred from reporting to it

condition: Minimum capital a commercial bank must hold
what_varies: the amount
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Minimum capital a microfinance bank must hold
what_varies: the amount

condition: Whether exchange and microfinance activities may be combined
what_varies: allowed or prohibited

condition: How much a microfinance bank may lend to one borrower
what_varies: the ceiling

condition: Whether banks and money exchangers must have audited financial statements
what_varies: required or not

condition: Who sets interest rates on deposits
what_varies: who sets them

condition: Whether nonbank lenders are regulated
what_varies: regulated or not

condition: Which laws govern banking and money exchange
what_varies: the laws

condition: Whether buyers can use a bank's or wallet's mobile app
what_varies: working, stopped for technical reasons, or blocked
note: Part C: the Kuraimi apps' stoppages, and the blocking of the apps of banks that moved their head offices to Aden. The same article gives both accounts of January 2026 (blocked, YQ-C385; a technical fault, YQ-C386).

condition: Whether a merchant can send and receive international commercial transfers through a bank
what_varies: available or not

condition: Whether a business can run its bank account through electronic services
what_varies: available or not

condition: Whether banks run one system across the government-held and Houthi-held areas
what_varies: one system, or separate systems for each area

condition: Who performs banking tasks
what_varies: banks, or exchange companies

condition: What services banks mainly offer
what_varies: the services

condition: Whether firms can get bank credit
what_varies: available or scarce, and on what terms

condition: What collateral lenders require
what_varies: the collateral

condition: Cost of bank credit
what_varies: the lending rate

condition: Cost of microfinance credit
what_varies: the interest rate

condition: Whether lenders can check borrowers' credit history
what_varies: the depth of credit information

condition: Whether SME loans can be guaranteed
what_varies: whether a guarantee scheme operates

condition: What a business needs to open a bank account
what_varies: the documents

condition: Whether one may buy assets seized from banks
what_varies: valid, or invalid and sanctionable

condition: Which transfer networks exchange companies and banks may or must use for domestic transfers
what_varies: the unified network (UNMONEY) required, allowed or barred; the companies' and banks' own networks allowed or closed; Kuraimi Express barred
note: Joins parts A, C, D and E: the Aden central bank's network rules, the Sana'a side's bans on the unified network and on Kuraimi Express, and part D's 'how domestic money transfers can be made' for its rows stating these rules. Sources date the unified network's mandate to February 2024, June 2024 and July 2024.

condition: Who takes part in the unified money transfer network
what_varies: the banks, exchange companies and e-wallets linked to it, its owners, and whether it is running, planned or being restructured
note: Joins parts C, D and E. YQ-C435 is the Sana'a side's planned network.

condition: Through which channels money is moved within Yemen in practice
what_varies: the main channels (exchange and hawala networks, Kuraimi Express, banks) and how far they are supervised
note: Joins parts D and E, including part E's 'Informal money transfer (hawala) available'.

condition: Through which channels remittances from abroad reach Yemen
what_varies: the main channels (banks, international transfer companies, exchange companies, hawala, informal networks) and their shares
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Whether money can be sent between areas held by different parties
what_varies: possible or stopped, and through whom
note: Joins parts C and D.

condition: Whether cash and foreign currency may be moved from one side's area to the other
what_varies: allowed, limited or banned
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Whether digital payments work across the lines of control
what_varies: working, or a barrier for lack of interoperability

condition: Fee for sending money between areas held by different parties
what_varies: the fee or loss, as a share or amount, by direction
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Fee for domestic money transfers
what_varies: the fee level, or that it has risen
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Currency in which transfers between areas are priced
what_varies: the rial, or an intermediate foreign currency

condition: How exchange companies settle transfers between areas
what_varies: the currency of settlement

condition: How much may be sent in one money transfer through exchangers and agents
what_varies: the ceiling per transfer, per customer or between governorates, or none
note: Joins parts D, E and F.

condition: Who may pay out remittances from abroad
what_varies: which banks, exchange companies and agents are allowed
note: Joins parts C, D and E: the Aden central bank's decision of May 2024 (YQ-D031, YQ-D032), its 2024 resolution (YQ-E810) and the Sana'a central bank's circular of March 2024 (YQ-C393).

condition: Currency in which remittances from abroad are paid out
what_varies: in the currency sent, in rials, in Saudi riyals, or not in US dollars
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Whether a buyer can send and receive international money transfers through a service
what_varies: available or not at the service named, and through which transfer companies (Western Union, MoneyGram, Ria, stablecoins)
note: Joins parts A, C, D and E: each provider's own service, and the corridor's transfer companies (YQ-A008). Also wallets' receipt of transfers from abroad (parts C and E). The Cash wallet's pages disagree: a possible future addition (YQ-C041) and available (YQ-C169).

condition: Whether banks can receive wire transfers from abroad
what_varies: direct, through intermediaries, costlier or slower

condition: How readily remittances from abroad reach each area
what_varies: the share of inflows, access to formal services, cost and speed, and whether banks can pay out
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Cost of sending money to Yemen from abroad
what_varies: the cost (an average, a corridor's, a channel's or a provider's)
note: Joins parts A, D and E. Its rows give averages, channel ranges and provider figures from different surveys.

condition: Currencies of transfers into Yemen through banks
what_varies: the currencies

condition: Whether international payment services can be used for payments from or to Yemen
what_varies: available, send only, or unavailable at the service named
note: Joins parts D and E. Wise's two pages disagree on Wise (YQ-E580, YQ-E581), and sources differ on PayPal (YQ-D634, YQ-E579, YQ-E728). YQ-E582 is a request, open on the capture date, to add WooPayments for Yemeni businesses.

condition: Whether and how an exchange business must renew its licence
what_varies: renewal required, by when and through which channel
note: Joins parts B and F; all rest on the Sana'a central bank's announcement of early 2026.

condition: Which exchange businesses are licensed to operate
what_varies: the licensed list, or only those on it
note: Joins parts D and F.

condition: Who may obtain an exchange licence
what_varies: the capital required and limits on new licences and branches by area
note: Joins parts D and E.

condition: Whether customers of a failed exchange company are compensated from its licence guarantee
what_varies: compensated or not

condition: How many exchange businesses work without a licence
what_varies: the number or share of unlicensed exchange businesses
note: Joins parts D and E. Sources differ: YQ-D211 and YQ-D428 count about 800 of 1,350 exchange outlets as unlicensed; YQ-E770 calls the 1,350 licensed and the 800 additional.

condition: How many exchange businesses operate
what_varies: the number of exchange companies, establishments and agents
note: Joins parts A, D and E. Sources give different counts for Aden and Sana'a in 2023 (part D's notes).

condition: What an exchange company closed by the central bank must do to resume
what_varies: what it must pay or do

condition: Whether an exchange company may move its operations out of the Houthi-held areas
what_varies: allowed or prevented

condition: Whether exchange companies may hold customer accounts and take deposits
what_varies: allowed or prohibited, and whether they do so in practice
note: Joins parts D, E and F.

condition: What a money exchanger may do under the exchange law
what_varies: the activities allowed and barred

condition: What exchange companies must do with unclaimed transfers
what_varies: report them, to whom and by when

condition: What money exchangers must report to the central bank
what_varies: the data and how often

condition: How closely the central bank supervises exchange companies and transfers
what_varies: strict supervision, electronic tracking of transfers, inspections, or minimal or disabled oversight
note: Joins parts A, D and E, including part A's central bank monitoring of transfers. YQ-A035 and YQ-E893 report the same article.

condition: Whether exchange companies may hold accounts with each other
what_varies: allowed or prohibited

condition: Which identity documents a customer must show for a financial transaction or transfer
what_varies: the documents and data required, and whether expired cards are accepted
note: Joins parts B, E and F, including the civil registry authority's rule on which identity cards are valid (YQ-B014). YQ-B013 and YQ-F151 rest on the same circular.

condition: What a recipient must present to collect a money transfer in cash
what_varies: the identification required, by amount
note: Joins parts E and F.

condition: In what form a customer may draw balances and transfers held at exchange firms
what_varies: the form and currency

condition: Whether exchange firms may charge a commission for paying out in cash
what_varies: allowed or not

condition: Whether a buyer can send money within Yemen through a transfer network
what_varies: available or not at the service named
note: Joins parts C and D.

condition: Whether buyers have digital transfers available
what_varies: available or not, and to whom

condition: What a bank's transfer agencies offer customers
what_varies: the services offered

condition: Whether a buyer can pay for purchases at shops from a phone wallet or bank app
what_varies: available or not at the service named (how: points of sale, store codes, QR)
note: Joins parts C, D and E: each wallet's or bank app's payments at merchants (Hasseb, merchant payments, points of sale). Online purchases, bills and transfers to persons are separate conditions, since a service can offer one and not another; rows listing a wallet's whole range of services are in the condition on which services a wallet offers.

condition: Whether a buyer can pay for online purchases from a phone wallet or bank app
what_varies: available, coming later, or not, at the wallet or at the online store named (and which wallets the store accepts)
note: Joins parts C, D and E: wallets' online payment and online stores' acceptance of wallets. Also part D's rows on buyers paying online stores through a wallet or Haseb, and stores accepting them.

condition: Whether a buyer can pay bills and fees from a phone wallet or bank app
what_varies: available or not at the service named (the bills named are detail)
note: Joins parts A, C and D, including SabaCard's bill payments (YQ-A012) and billers' acceptance of wallets (YQ-C440, YQ-C565).

condition: Whether a buyer can send money to another person from a phone wallet or bank app
what_varies: available or not at the service named

condition: Whether a buyer can use a phone wallet without internet or a smartphone
what_varies: available by SMS or USSD or on basic phones, or the app needs internet
note: Joins parts C, D and E: part C's paying by SMS, paying without internet and use from a basic phone, which are the same availability.

condition: Whether a buyer can transfer money between different providers' wallets
what_varies: available or not, and through which link (WeNet, Wasel), at the service named or across the market
note: Joins parts C, D and E.

condition: Whether a buyer can send money from a phone wallet to someone without one
what_varies: available or not, and how the recipient collects
note: Joins parts C and E.

condition: What happens to a wallet transfer to someone without a wallet that is not collected
